### Define a Static robots.txt File

Source: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/01-metadata/robots.mdx

Place a static `robots.txt` file in the `app` directory root to specify crawling rules for search engine bots.

```txt
User-Agent: *
Allow: /
Disallow: /private/

Sitemap: https://acme.com/sitemap.xml
```

--------------------------------

### Metadata collection: what gets collected at each level

Source: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/next/src/build/webpack/loaders/metadata/discover.ts

Shows icon, apple, openGraph, and twitter are always collected from any directory level, while favicon and manifest are only collected at root level (isRootLayoutOrRootPage=true). This directly answers where these files can live: icon.tsx, apple-icon.tsx, opengraph-image.tsx at any level inside a route group; manifest.ts only at the route group root (since groups act as root when no top-level layout exists).

```typescript
  // Intentionally make these serial to reuse directory access cache.
  await collectIconModuleIfExists('icon')
  await collectIconModuleIfExists('apple')
  await collectIconModuleIfExists('openGraph')
  await collectIconModuleIfExists('twitter')
  if (isRootLayoutOrRootPage) {
    await collectIconModuleIfExists('favicon')
    await collectIconModuleIfExists('manifest')
  }
```

--------------------------------

### Define Metadata in Root Layout (TypeScript/JavaScript)

Source: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/layout.mdx

Use the `metadata` object in `layout.tsx` or `layout.js` to configure page metadata like title. Avoid manually adding `<head>` tags.

```tsx
import type { Metadata } from 'next'

export const metadata: Metadata = {
  title: 'Next.js',
}

export default function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return '...'
}
```

```jsx
export const metadata = {
  title: 'Next.js',
}

export default function Layout({ children }) {
  return '...'
}
```

### Metadata Files API Reference

Source: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/01-metadata/index.mdx

Metadata file conventions allow defining file-based metadata by adding special metadata files to route segments.

--------------------------------

### public Folder > Robots, Favicons, and others

Source: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/public-folder.mdx

For static metadata files like `robots.txt` and `favicon.ico` within the App Router, it is recommended to use special metadata files located inside the `app` folder instead of the `public` folder.

---
name: gotcha-metadata-routes-route-groups
description: Next.js registers robots.ts only at the app root, but sitemap.ts works nested — so the two need opposite proxy handling in bartr's site-* layout
metadata:
  type: project
---

Next.js metadata file conventions are **not** uniformly nestable, and bartr's
`site-marketing` / `site-app` / `site-admin` physical-path layout collides with
that asymmetry:

- `app/site-marketing/sitemap.ts` **does** register — it builds a real route at
  `/site-marketing/sitemap.xml` (visible in `app-paths-manifest.json` and in
  `pnpm build` output).
- `app/site-marketing/robots.ts` **does not** register. `robots.ts` is a
  root-only convention; nested, it is silently dead code — no route, no build
  warning. It sat there unnoticed until 2026-08-10.

Consequence for `proxy.ts`: the two need *opposite* treatment.

- `/sitemap.xml` must be **in** the matcher and must survive
  `skipsRouteGroupRewrite` (which otherwise drops anything containing a `.`),
  so the proxy can rewrite it into the marketing route group. It is also
  gated on `routeGroup === "site-marketing"`, and listed in
  `config/authkit.config.ts` `unauthenticatedPaths` so app/admin hosts return a
  clean 404 instead of a 307 to sign-in.
- `/robots.txt` must stay **excluded** from the matcher and lives at
  `app/robots.ts`, serving every host with no rewrite at all.

**Why:** the "one line, remove both from the matcher exclusion" fix looks right
and is wrong twice over — `skipsRouteGroupRewrite`'s `pathname.includes(".")`
guard also has to be taught about it, and for robots the rewrite target never
existed in the first place.

**How to apply:** before adding any metadata route under a `site-*` folder,
check `pnpm build`'s route list for it. If it does not appear, the convention is
root-only — put the file at `app/` and leave the path out of the proxy matcher.
Verify per host with `curl -H "Host: www.localhost:3033"` against `pnpm dev`;
the dev tunnel is useless for this because Cloudflare serves its own managed
`robots.txt` at the edge and never reaches Next.js.

Related: [[gotcha-admin-subdomain-links]] (the same site-* physical-path
weirdness, seen from the link side).
